B2.name: FRC.Causality.no_causal_root
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, first clause): `c² = ν` makes `ν` a square, so a nonsquare `ν` has no root.

B2.name: FRC.Causality.neg_sq_is_square
B2.doc: 3:B2 (the consequence): when `−1` is a square (`card F ≢ 3 mod 4`) so is `−c²`, and every coefficient of `−c² t² + x² + y² + z²` lies in the class of squares — a Euclidean form for every `c ≠ 0`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.no_causal_root
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, first clause) — `c² = ν` makes `ν` a square, so a nonsquare `ν` has no root `c`.

B2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.neg_sq_is_square
B2.doc: 3:B2 (Thm. nonexistence, the consequence) — `−c²` is a square on every shell: `−c² = (i·c)²` with `i² = −1`; so with `c ≠ 0` every coefficient of `−c² t² + x² + y² + z²` is a square and the form is Euclidean.

B3.name: FRC.Causality.absorb
B3.doc: 3:B3 (Lemma absorption): coefficients `a_i = w_i² a_0` are absorbed by `x_i ↦ w_i x_i`.

B3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.absorb
B3.doc: 3:B3 (Lemma absorption) — if `a_i = w_i² a_0` for `i = 1, 2, 3` then `a_0 x_0² + a_1 x_1² + a_2 x_2² + a_3 x_3² = a_0 (x_0² + (w_1 x_1)² + (w_2 x_2)² + (w_3 x_3)²)`: a common square class is absorbed by the rescaling `x_i ↦ w_i x_i`, with no square root of `a_0` itself required.

B4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null13
B4.doc: 3:B4, 3:D1 [value] — the null cone of `Q_2` on `𝔽₁₃` has `2041 = 13³ − 13² + 13` points: the elliptic type.

B4.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.euclid13
B4.doc: 3:B4 [value] — the Euclidean form (`ν = 1`) on `𝔽₁₃` has `2353 = 13³ + 13² − 13` zeros: the hyperbolic type.

B5.name: FRC.Causality.aniso_tx
B5.doc: 3:B5: `x² − ν t²` is anisotropic for a nonsquare `ν`.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.aniso_tx
B5.doc: 3:B5 — the plane `x² − ν t²` is anisotropic when `ν` is a nonsquare: `x² = ν t²` forces `t = x = 0` (else `ν = (x/t)²`). This is the Witt kernel of the Lorentzian form, its index one.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null_yz
B5.doc: 3:B5 — the `(y, z)`-plane `y² + z²` is hyperbolic on every shell: `(1, i)` is null.

B5.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null_tx_of_square
B5.doc: 3:B5 — for a square `ν = w²` the `(t, x)`-plane is hyperbolic too: `(1, w)` is null; the form is then `H ⊥ H`, Witt index two — the Euclidean type.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_preserves
C2.doc: 3:C2 (the finite Lorentz boost): `Λ(γ, b) = !![γ, b; νb, γ]` with `γ² − νb² = 1` preserves `x² − ν t²`.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_comp
C2.doc: 3:C2: the boosts compose as the norm-one elements of `F(√ν)` multiply.

C2.name: FRC.Causality.boost_orthogonal
C2.doc: 3:C2: `Λ(γ, b)` is orthogonal for the Gram matrix `diag(−ν, 1)` of `Q_ν`: `Λᵀ G Λ = G`.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.boost_preserves
C2.doc: 3:C2 (the finite Lorentz boost) — with `γ² − νb² = 1`, `Λ(γ, b)` preserves `x² − ν t²` exactly, on every shell.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.boost_comp_t
C2.doc: 3:C2 — boosts compose as their parameters multiply in `K`: `Λ(γ₁, b₁) Λ(γ₂, b₂) = Λ(γ₁γ₂ + νb₁b₂, γ₁b₂ + b₁γ₂)`, the `t`-row.

C2.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.norm_one_mul
C2.doc: 3:C2 — the norm-one elements form a group: `N(z₁z₂) = N(z₁)N(z₂) = 1`.

C3.name: FRC.Causality.gamma_ne_zero
C3.doc: 3:C3: `γ ≠ 0` on every boost of the Lorentzian plane (`γ = 0` would make `ν = (i/b)²`).

C3.name: FRC.Causality.gamma_velocity
C3.doc: 3:C3: the velocity `v = −νb/γ` satisfies `γ² (ν − v²) = ν` — `γ = 1/√(1 − β²)` with `β² = v²/ν`.

C3.name: FRC.Causality.velocity_addition
C3.doc: 3:C3 (Einstein's addition law, exact): `v₁₂ (ν + v₁v₂) = ν (v₁ + v₂)`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gamma_ne_zero
C3.doc: 3:C3 — `γ ≠ 0` on every boost of the Lorentzian plane: `γ = 0` would give `ν b² = −1`, i.e. `ν = (i/b)²`, a square.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.gamma_velocity
C3.doc: 3:C3 — the velocity of the boost, `v = −νb/γ` (`vγ = −νb`), satisfies `γ² (ν − v²) = ν`: the finite form of `γ = 1/√(1 − β²)` with `β² = v²/ν`.

C3.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.velocity_addition
C3.doc: 3:C3 (the velocity addition law) — for boosts with velocities `v₁, v₂` (`v_i γ_i = −ν b_i`) and the composed boost's velocity `v₁₂`, `v₁₂ (ν + v₁v₂) = ν (v₁ + v₂)`: Einstein's law `v₁₂ = (v₁ + v₂)/(1 + v₁v₂/ν)`, exact.

D1.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.null13
D1.doc: 3:B4, 3:D1 [value] — the null cone of `Q_2` on `𝔽₁₃` has `2041 = 13³ − 13² + 13` points: the elliptic type.
